transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-11-09
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Alex Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jordan Patel (Product), Tessa Nguyen (Solutions) -- Evan Morris (StrataConnect), Priya Singh (StrataConnect CTO), Liam O'Connor (Solutions Architect), Hana Park (Security)

Summary:
Quick partner intro and discovery focused on hybrid integration options (hosted API vs dedicated vs private VPC), pilot framing, security expectations, and initial benchmarking scope. Customer is evaluating GPU partners to provide low-latency inference to enterprise customers and wants predictable costs and auditability.

Topics:
- Integration patterns (API vs VPC vs on-prem)
- Performance/cost tradeoffs (latency, batching, quantization)
- Security/compliance (KMS, audit logs, SSO)
- Pilot scope and success criteria

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everybody thanks for joining, um i'm Maya from Redwood AE, i'll kick us off. can folks do quick intros?
[00:08] Evan Morris: yeah evan here, head of cloud partnerships at strata connect, thanks for setting this up.
[00:13] Priya Singh: priya, cto. we're exploring partners for gpu-backed inference for our managed ai offering.
[00:18] Alex Ruiz: alex, solutions engineer - i'll lead on the technical side, especially around performance and networking.
[00:22] Liam O'Connor: liam, solutions architect. i'll own the integration with our control plane.
[00:26] Hana Park: hana, security lead - i'll focus on compliance and kms/keys.
[00:30] Jordan Patel: jordan from product, mostly listening for roadmap fit.
[00:34] Maya Chen: great. high level: redwood is a developer-first inference platform that supports hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, and private vpc/on-prem deployments. our goal in this call is to understand strata connect's constraints and propose a pilot that's realistic and measurable.
[00:52] Priya Singh: quick context — our customers run low-latency chat assistants and real-time document search. we need p95 latency below 200ms for short sequences, and for longer flows we care about throughput and cost. also enterprise customers need audit logs and key control.
[01:10] Alex Ruiz: okay thanks. can you share current stack? are you using a managed cloud GPU provider today or DIY?
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: right now it's kind of hybrid. we have some on-prem for regulated clients, but most is on CloudAI spot instances. it's been painful around tail latency and preemptions. that's why we're looking at dedicated pools or a partner with predictable SLOs.
[01:35] Evan Morris: and we have a wide tenancy of tenants, so multitenancy isolation is a must. data residency for eu customers is also a constraint.
[01:44] Maya Chen: yep makes sense. two patterns we propose: 1) Dedicated reserved pools per tenancy group — good for SLOs and isolation; 2) Private VPC peering where your control plane talks to our private control plane — gives you full network isolation. hosted api is an option for dev/onboard but less likely for regulated clients.
[02:05] Priya Singh: can you clarify the private vpc option? is the control plane still hosted?
[02:12] Alex Ruiz: short answer: yes, the control plane is customer-managed in Private — think of a private control plane that we help deploy into your VPC. data plane can be in your region, and you can bring your own KMS/HSM. there are variants: fully on-prem package if needed.
[02:30] Hana Park: important: we need to know what logs are exported, retention windows, and how KMS integration works. we have SOC2 and some customers require ISO certs.
[02:39] Tessa Nguyen: we'll share our security pack. it includes SOC2 type II reports, KMS integration docs, SSO/SAML flows, RBAC models, and audit log examples.
[02:49] Priya Singh: thanks, that'll help. on perf — are there known throughput numbers for, say, 2x40b models with batching? our median sequence is ~120 tokens.
[02:58] Alex Ruiz: rough numbers vary by quantization and kernel selection; for 40b-class models on A100-style GPUs, it's about X tokens/s with continuous batching — but i'd like to run your traces. our optimize toolkit recommends quant profiles based on your distribution to hit cost latency tradeoffs.
[03:20] Liam O'Connor: can you do live benchmarking with our traces? preemptions have been our main problem on spot.
[03:25] Alex Ruiz: yes, we can run an end-to-end benchmark in a sandbox — that's one of the action items. we typically ask for anonymized request traces and a sample prompt set. we can mirror your sequence length distribution and concurrency.
[03:39] Evan Morris: what's the typical pilot duration? we want to show this to 3 customers fast.
[03:44] Maya Chen: recommend 2-3 weeks for a dedicated pilot: 1 week to provision and baseline, 1 week for load and edge cases, final week to validate SLOs and cost. we can compress if you have good readiness.
[03:57] Priya Singh: cost question — how transparent is pricing? we need predictable unit economics for our product pricing.
[04:04] Jordan Patel: we price on usage + reserved capacity for Dedicated. we can show token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards so you can model your margins.
[04:14] Liam O'Connor: on the routing bit, do you support smart routing by region and fallback to smaller models if capacity spikes?
[04:20] Alex Ruiz: yes, smart routing is a core feature — policies for latency/cost/region; fallback to compatible quantized variants or smaller model revisions. automatic fallback helps maintain uptime.
[04:32] Hana Park: what about encryption in transit? and is KV cache stored in customer network? we want keys not shared.
[04:39] Alex Ruiz: data in transit is TLS; KV cache can be kept within your VPC for private deployments. with Private we can use your KMS so keys never leave your control. for hosted we use our managed KMS but support customer-managed keys for enterprise tiers.
[04:56] Evan Morris: any gotchas for peering and egress costs? some clouds charge a lot for cross-region traffic.
[05:02] Tessa Nguyen: we'll include recommended network topologies and egress best practices in the pack — and outline what traffic remains in-region.
[05:11] Priya Singh: we have internal SI partners that handle on-prem install — will Redwood work with them?
[05:16] Maya Chen: yes, we often collaborate with integrators. we can align on an integration runbook and a contact plan.
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: success criteria for pilot: 95th percentile latency under 250ms for short chat flows, less than 10% cost increase vs baseline with improved predictability, and full audit log delivery to our SIEM.
[05:36] Jordan Patel: that's a solid starting point. we should also add model quality regressions not to exceed X% on our evals — we can propose a prompt set comparison.
[05:48] Alex Ruiz: quick note on evaluation: Redwood Optimize can run automated evals tied to prompt sets and alert on regressions — we'll demo that if you want.
[05:58] Evan Morris: yes please.
[06:01] Priya Singh: timeline — we aim to pick a partner within 3 weeks and run pilots in december. is that realistic?
[06:08] Maya Chen: yes, if we get traces and approvals quickly we can provision a pilot early december. we'll need contracts for Dedicated reserved capacity if that's selected.
[06:18] Hana Park: i'll want a list of data flows and where PII might transit.
[06:22] Tessa Nguyen: understood — we'll send a data flow template.
[06:25] Liam O'Connor: small question: how do you handle multi-tenant separation inside a dedicated pool?
[06:31] Alex Ruiz: we support tenant pinning and namespace-level isolation plus workload-level RBAC. for extra isolation we can allocate dedicated GPU nodes per tenant group.
[06:42] Priya Singh: are there examples of customers who ran similar pilots?
[06:45] Maya Chen: yes, a couple of fintech and health-tech partners — we can share sanitized case studies in the pack.
[06:52] Evan Morris: any potential blockers we should flag internally?
[06:55] Maya Chen: typically network approval and KMS legal review take the longest — hence recommend starting security review asap.
[07:02] Priya Singh: ok makes sense.
[07:05] Jordan Patel: recap and next steps?
[07:08] Maya Chen: recap: 1) Redwood to share SOC2/security pack, network diagrams, and KMS options (Tessa). 2) Strata to send anonymized request traces and sequence distribution (Priya). 3) Redwood to provision Dedicated pilot and run benchmarks (Alex). 4) Schedule VPC deep-dive with Hana and Alex — target next week. 5) Redwood to send SOW + pricing ranges.
[07:32] Priya Singh: sounds good.
[07:35] Evan Morris: thanks everyone, excited to move fast.
[07:38] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the pack.
[07:42] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: some model/product names and acronyms may be imperfect; timestamps approximate.
